ciInventory.name: Start server and run smoke
ciInventory.command:
set -euo pipefail
nohup ./bin/paimos serve >"$RUNNER_TEMP/aeon.log" 2>&1 &
echo $! >"$RUNNER_TEMP/aeon.pid"
ready=0
for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
  if curl -sf "$BASE_URL/api/health" >/dev/null; then
    ready=1
    break
  fi
  sleep 1
done
if [ "$ready" -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "server did not become ready" >&2
  cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/aeon.log" >&2 || true
  exit 1
fi
npm run e2e --prefix web

integrationNotes: AEON-676: OPS-257 runner/workflow and coverage guard integrated from dc61efd76ad7263749c3b70a515aad5e40df60ba. The clipped-names-and-preferences group gates clip-tip, aeon-632b-clip, key-trim and model-prefs once, with no clip-tip exclusion. The touch layout fix passed six variants x20 locally; hosted execution of this integrated revision still needs coordinator CI. Weights for these 247 tests remain scheduling estimates: clip-tip uses the complete local serial run plus a 20 percent margin; the other three use native test counts. Hosted runtimes remain unmeasured.

OPS: group remaining-ui is ungated (gate:false). These 164 specs were never part of the CI gate and have no measured timing; the gate keeps today's measured coverage so the merge queue gets faster, not wider. Run them with --all (ci:web:shard -- --all i/N); a follow-up ticket measures them and decides whether they gate.
The old workflow discovers no full-suite step: it explicitly selects 48 UI specs (37 in web). The manifest covers all 213 UI specs once; 165 have no measured CI step duration.

Remove the replaced browser invocations, including overlaps in footer/status/e2e jobs, when wiring the full UI shards. Keep their other checks and collect evidence from the shards. Otherwise those old jobs still duplicate manifest coverage.
Keep e2e/smoke.spec.ts and browser lifecycle probes in e2e; neither is part of the UI spec universe.

Upload test-results/ci-web, screenshot directories under RUNNER_TEMP, and .agent-shots/planning + .agent-shots/queue from shards. Run --check --shards 12 and ci:web:shard:test in setup before browsers.

Flake guard can request --last-failed (per-group last-run state) or --test-list /absolute/failures.txt (native Playwright test-list format). Empty groups succeed only during these failure-only selections.

PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_FILE enables per-group JSON reports plus one combined report at that path; --reporter=json is also accepted. Prior report bytes are invalidated before launch so startup failure/interruption cannot reuse green evidence.

Shard assignment is based on file names and timing weights only; groups execute sequentially with their own original policies. Weights for the 165 newly covered specs are estimates; hosted measurement is needed before claiming the 5-minute target.

RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT must be github-hosted for execution; it is GitHub Actions built-in runner metadata. Local --list/--check remain browser-free. --last-failed preflights per-group state and refuses missing/invalid state instead of Playwright's full-selection fallback.

AEON-679 rule B: removed low-value capture, polish, duplicate scan and literal geometry cases; mixed protected cases remain. Changed spec listedTests use native collection; weights are proportional scheduling estimates, not measured runtime savings. Historical timingSource and ciInventory remain provenance only. The optional historical/current release-list screenshot jobs were retired with their capture case.

OPS-257 round 3: the tier runner forces --workers=1. tierWeights converts historical per-file allocations from measured N-worker steps to N * weightSeconds serial estimates; local-serial and unmeasured test-count estimates stay unchanged. Original exact-spec weights, launch policies, gated membership and tier classifications are preserved. On the committed full-gate tier ledger, corrected LPT bins estimate 367.9–371.8 seconds of tests (max/median 1.01, previously 266.1–496.5 seconds under the same serial model). These are scheduling estimates derived from historical step timings, not new per-spec hosted measurements. Run 37333283440 had 5.3–10.4 minute jobs; runner setup, native collection and group launches remain additional costs.

OPS-257 fix1: hosted per-case tierTiming replaces serial historical allocations for 58 measured files. aeon-632b-clip has 39 cases / 432.3 seconds including group overhead: keep one worker and schedule it alone; no gated membership or launch flags change. Unmeasured files keep explicit historical estimates; the next hosted run must validate runner and native collection costs.

AEON-697: Needs attention gates once in its own serial, trace-preserving group. listedTests comes from native collection; weightSeconds uses the existing unmeasured seconds/test estimate, not hosted runtime evidence.

OPS-257 round 4 L3: refresh measured per-case browser and per-owner Go/unit costs from full PR run 37377299349 (b2f9935a4264e932eae0fa2acd07c71e8d1fc417). The 39 clip cases split into planning/touch (27) and settings/rules (12), with shared imported fixtures and unchanged policies/tiers. Browser costs include group and tier execution residuals; each clip half conservatively retains the full original launch overhead. Go costs include terminal package elapsed plus each shard's residual native enumeration/launch time shared equally by its owners. Unit costs include Vitest elapsed or top-level Node durations plus shared residual launch time. Runner setup and unit shard 1's separate safety checks are excluded; hosted CI must validate total wall time. Exact-spec weightSeconds retain their historical allocation model; only the old clip allocation is divided proportionally between the two new files. The full-gate tier scheduler uses the refreshed tierTiming costs. Unit tie preference assigns shard 1 last on equal loads, moving the largest file to shard 2 without estimating the separate safety-check duration.

AEON-878: models-board-controls stays gated at 1s, the largest weight that keeps the twelve-shard prior maximum under 300 (1.1s reaches 300.01). The 12 screenshot cases moved to ungated models-board-evidence.spec.ts carry the other 15s of the original 16s estimate. Behavior cases remain in the gate.

AEON-903: Phone approvals has seven native cases. The local one-worker run passed all seven in 7.480 seconds including browser/server startup; aeon-903-local-serial-wall records that observation as a scheduling estimate, not a hosted-runtime promise.

AEON-1024: split clip-tip into lifecycle, disclosure, overflow and touch owners; split aeon-632b planning from restricted-group touch; split no-shift agents from dialogs and guard checks. Native before/after catalogues preserve all 224 executable cases, original policies and tiers. Tier scheduling costs derive from run 37377299349 per-case duration; historical exact-spec weight budgets are redistributed in proportion to these costs; each new file retains its full original owner residual. Cases added since that run retain an explicit owner-average estimate. The baseline and executable equality/weight proof live in scripts/ci/slow-owner-baseline.json and scripts/test-tiers/slow-owners.mjs. No shard count or worker count changes.

AEON-1040 fix2: replace model-prefs' stale 29-second local estimate with the complete three-case hosted measurement from PR #445 run 37948687065 attempt 1 (merge SHA 63841419452e1bfb206e6505b8051b8083527654, head d9287d401d5faee2223a04d7d805f84509c46c8b). All three cases passed once in web-shard-9-stable-controls-combined.json. Native durations total 5.222 seconds; apportioned launch overhead adds 0.112131 seconds (3 of 80 launch cases), and remaining shard collection/planning overhead adds 0.231546 seconds (3 of 142 shard cases). tierTiming retains their 5.565677-second total; weightSeconds rounds that total with a 20% margin up to 7 seconds. This restores the merged twelve-shard prior estimate budget using runtime evidence; coverage, tiers, launch policies, shard/worker counts and budget assertions remain unchanged.

AEON-1270: native-expert-stream has twelve cases in stable-controls. The prior guarded one-worker run passed all twelve in 7.3 seconds including startup; the ten-second weight is a conservative scheduling estimate from that observation, not a hosted-runtime promise. Six authority/replay/terminal behavior cases are ESSENTIAL; six viewport/theme cases are newly classified NIGHTLY.

AEON-1327: nightly catalogue shards pack from nightlyTiming, measured on hosted run 38488051180. Completed batches contribute wall time apportioned by Playwright case duration. theme-agents (650s), clip-tip-touch (200s), ticket-graph-view (90s) and work-surfaces-fix4 (120s) were still running when the 20-minute step died, so those four keep a conservative full-file estimate. settings-shared and work-surfaces-fix2 were not in that run and keep their tierTiming estimate. PR and merge-group packing stays on tierTiming. The 24-shard estimate peaks near 14.9 minutes, so the nightly execution cap stays 20 minutes.

AEON-1309: native-session-program.spec.ts has a nightlyTiming row for all nine cases. Its 60 seconds reuse the declared conservative scheduling estimate; this is not a measurement from run 38488051180. The ESSENTIAL tier, gate membership and historical weight are unchanged.

tierTimingSource.basis: Median native first-pass result.duration seconds per current gated browser case from three green full merge-group runs (all 12 shard artifacts per run). Native owner seconds sum those per-case medians; split-owner tier estimates retain their complete catalogue count and extrapolate unmeasured cases using the measured owner mean; the unchanged serial tier planner scales partial and nightly selections by selected case count. Nightly-only owners retain prior estimates. Launch and shard residuals are measured separately, never multiplied by owner or case count in the wall prediction. Historical exact-spec weightSeconds, membership and launch policies are unchanged.

timingSource.allocation: For each measured step, split its duration proportionally to the listed test count of each original spec. Duplicate specs retain the first dedicated owner. Unmeasured specs use their listed test count times the median measured step seconds/test: an estimate, not runtime evidence.

testCollection.note: Browser-free native collection; each final group was also collected separately to verify exact files/config/flags. Counts are embedded per spec so CI does not need tmp artifacts.
